newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht higher, interbank rate steady late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht higher, interbank rate steady late.

text.p: The baht was traded slightly higher against the dollar in late thin trade on Wednesday in line with the U.S. unit's weakness abroad, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 26.068/26.073 near the close compared with 26.075/26.080 earlier.
The mid-rate was set at 26.08 per dollar against 26.04 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the news that Thai exports in February contracted by 5.5 percent did not affect the baht sentiment as the market had not expected any major rebound of exports in the near term.

"There was not any impact on the market from the negative export growth in February. Our exports have been in the doldrums for several months and will take time to pick up," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday the exports in February contracted 5.5 percent year on year mostly due to a drop in agricultural commodities.
He also attributed sluggish trade in February to several holidays during the month.
Dealers said the overall baht/dollar spot trade remained sluggish on lack of fresh news and quiet dollar abroad.
The overnight interbank rate was steady at 8.00 percent in late trade compared with 8.00-8.50 in early morning, dealers said.
Dealers said the liqudity was slightly tighter than earlier this week because some banks began to build up their cash reserves for the next reserve requirement.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded at 6.00/6.50 satangs late, unchanged from early morning trade.
